firm.name: Velstrand Research
firm.tagline: Independent research on the European battery value chain
about: Velstrand Research is an independent research firm covering the European battery value chain, from lithium supply to cell manufacturing and gigafactory build-out.
Our analysts combine plant-level shipment data, customs records and interviews with industry contacts to publish proprietary market data used by investors, automakers and utilities.
Velstrand Research is a fictional company created for a hackathon demo. Every company name and every figure on this site is invented.

article.title: Who leads European battery manufacturing in 2025?
paragraphs: European lithium-ion cell output kept growing in 2025, but the gains were unevenly shared. The market leader extended its lead while the second largest player lost ground to a fast-growing challenger.
Central Europe remained the production heart of the continent, ahead of Germany and the Nordics. Utilisation rates improved everywhere but stay well below Asian benchmarks.
Our full report breaks down market share by manufacturer, output and utilisation by country, and explains our methodology.

sections.title: Executive summary
paragraphs: European lithium-ion cell output reached 235.6 GWh in 2025, up 18.7% year on year.
The five largest manufacturers held 88.9% of European output. Aurelion Cells extended its lead to 31.4% of the market, while Kestrel Energy Storage slipped to 22.7%.
Brightwell Power was the fastest-growing manufacturer, gaining 3.4 points of market share.

sections.title: Market share by manufacturer
paragraphs: Share of European lithium-ion cell output by manufacturer, 2025, and change versus 2024 in percentage points.

sections.title: Output and utilisation by country
paragraphs: Lithium-ion cell output and average plant utilisation by country, 2025. Poland alone produced 86.3 GWh.

sections.title: Methodology
paragraphs: Market shares are computed on cell output in GWh, not on revenue. Output is estimated from plant-level shipment data for 27 production sites, cross-checked with customs records.
We conducted 43 interviews with plant managers, procurement teams and equipment suppliers between January and November 2025. Figures are rounded to one decimal place.

reports.title: Lithium carbonate and hydroxide prices and costs, 2021-2025

article.title: Lithium prices: five years from boom to bust
paragraphs: Lithium prices went through a full cycle between 2021 and 2025: a spectacular spike, then a long decline that continued through 2025.
The hydroxide premium over carbonate narrowed but did not disappear. At current prices, the highest-cost hard rock producers are under pressure while brine producers keep comfortable margins.
Our full report gives annual spot prices for carbonate and hydroxide and a cash cost curve for the main producers.

sections.title: Executive summary
paragraphs: The average lithium carbonate spot price fell 18.5% in 2025 to 10,980 USD per tonne, far below the 2022 peak of 71,850 USD per tonne.
The hydroxide premium over carbonate averaged 660 USD per tonne in 2025.
Copperhead Spodumene, the highest-cost producer in our sample, operated with a cash cost of 8,315 USD per tonne.

sections.title: Spot prices by year
paragraphs: Average annual spot prices, battery grade, USD per tonne of lithium carbonate equivalent.

sections.title: Cash cost by producer
paragraphs: Estimated 2025 cash cost by producer, USD per tonne of lithium carbonate equivalent, and resource type.

sections.title: Methodology
paragraphs: Spot prices are averages of weekly assessments from 52 trading weeks per year, collected from 14 traders and converters.
Cash costs include mining, processing, royalties and logistics to port, and exclude sustaining capital. They are built bottom-up from company disclosures and 19 expert interviews.

article.title: Europe's gigafactory build-out: where the capacity really is
paragraphs: Announced gigafactory projects in Europe far exceed the capacity that is actually operational today. A handful of sites account for most of the real output.
The 2030 pipeline remains ambitious, but several projects have slipped and investment per GWh varies widely from one site to another.
Our full report lists operational capacity by site in 2025, the planned 2030 capacity and the associated investment.

sections.title: Executive summary
paragraphs: The five largest operational gigafactories in Europe had a combined nameplate capacity of 135.9 GWh per year in 2025.
The same five sites plan to reach 268.9 GWh per year by 2030, for a total announced investment of 16.96 billion EUR.

sections.title: Operational capacity by site, 2025
paragraphs: Nameplate capacity of operational sites at the end of 2025, GWh per year.

sections.title: Planned capacity and investment, 2030
paragraphs: Planned nameplate capacity in 2030 and announced investment for the same sites.

sections.title: Methodology
paragraphs: Operational capacity counts only production lines that shipped cells to customers in 2025. Announced projects without a final investment decision are excluded.
Data comes from site visits, operator disclosures and permits filed in 11 countries.

reports.title: Sodium-ion batteries in Europe, cost and adoption outlook 2025

article.title: Sodium-ion: a real alternative to lithium?
paragraphs: Sodium-ion cells are still more expensive than LFP today, but the gap is expected to close before the end of the decade.
Adoption will start in segments where energy density matters less, such as stationary storage and two-wheelers, well before mainstream electric cars.
Our full report compares cell costs with LFP and NMC and gives adoption forecasts by segment for 2030.

sections.title: Executive summary
paragraphs: Sodium-ion cells cost 87.4 USD per kWh in 2025, 21.6% more than LFP cells.
We expect sodium-ion to become cheaper than LFP by 2030, at 52.3 USD per kWh, and to reach 41.2% of new two-wheeler batteries in Europe.

sections.title: Cell cost comparison
paragraphs: Average cell cost by chemistry, USD per kWh, 2025 actual and 2030 forecast.

sections.title: Adoption forecast by segment, 2030
paragraphs: Forecast share of sodium-ion in new battery demand in Europe by segment, 2030.

sections.title: Methodology
paragraphs: Cell costs are bottom-up estimates built from material prices, plant throughput and yield assumptions validated with 8 cell manufacturers.
Adoption forecasts combine announced supply agreements with a demand model calibrated on 36 product launches.
